title: Pluggable agent algorithms and market clearing algorithms discovered from subclasses
approval_note: Requested and approved by the user on 2026-10-07 (PLAN.md 2.10): agent algorithms and market clearing algorithms are both defined as subclasses of a base class, discovered from the code and selectable in the simulation. The settlement rule (pay-as-bid / PTF) stays a separate choice.
depends_on: PLAN 2.9 merged (migration 0016_demand_profile_template). The migration of this item is 0017.
invariants: Existing results are unchanged: tests/runtime/test_result_fingerprint.py and the full suite stay green without changing expected values.

Keys of the existing agent algorithms are exactly the current AlgorithmType names: DDPG, RDPG, TD3, SAC, PPO, RANDOM, MARGINAL_COST, FIXED_MARKUP. Existing scenario YAML files (algorithm: DDPG) import unchanged.
Discovery imports modules lazily on first registry access (cached), not at Django start, to keep startup free of torch imports.

agent_algorithms.base_class: abmem/services/algorithms/base.py::BaseAgentAlgorithm gains ClassVars key: str, label: str, description: str, config_class: type[AlgorithmConfig] (is_learning and is_on_policy stay). The ClassVar algorithm_type is replaced by key.
agent_algorithms.registration: BaseAgentAlgorithm.__init_subclass__ registers every concrete subclass (not inspect.isabstract and a non-empty key) in a module-level registry. Duplicate key -> ImproperlyConfigured naming both classes. Key format ^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]{0,63}$.
agent_algorithms.discovery: registry.discover() imports every module of the package abmem.services.algorithms (pkgutil.iter_modules, skipping private modules starting with '_' and the subpackage optimization if it has no algorithms) once and caches the result. A module that fails to import is reported with its traceback in the error, not skipped silently.
registry_api: available_algorithms() -> tuple[AlgorithmInfo, ...]  (key, label, description, is_learning, is_on_policy, ordered: learning first then baselines, each by label)
get_algorithm_class(key: str) -> type[BaseAgentAlgorithm]  (KeyError listing known keys)
agent_algorithms.remove_static_tables: ALGORITHM_CLASS_PATHS, BASELINE_TYPES and algorithm_config.CONFIG_CLASSES are removed (or derived from the registry if a stable import is needed). Each existing algorithm class declares its own key, label, description, config_class.
agent_algorithms.models: Agent.algorithm_type, HPOStudy.algorithm_type, AlgorithmDefault.algorithm_type (unique) and PolicyCheckpoint's algorithm field become CharField(max_length=64) holding the key, default 'DDPG' where a default exists. Data migration maps the stored int through the old enum to its name and back in reverse. Keep the field names unless a rename is clearly simpler, and update every DB constraint that references them.
agent_algorithms.legacy_enum: abmem.models.enums.AlgorithmType stays only because historical migrations import it. Add a comment that live code must not use it. No live code path imports it after this change (grep check in a test).
agent_algorithms.consumers: Update every live use: library_service, scenario_yaml (validates the key with registry.is_known), forms_hpo, views, views_hpo, hpo_service (param_space_payload from the config class of the key), simulation context and service, checkpoints and persistence (stored key, warm start compares keys), run_analysis (labels from the registry), templatetags/abmem_choices (algorithm_choices from available_algorithms), templates and JS that send int values (they send keys now).
agent_algorithms.unknown_key: An agent whose key is no longer registered: list/forms show the key with an 'unavailable' badge, saving it again is rejected with a field error, a run start fails in SimulationContext.build with SimulationValidationError naming the agent and the key.

market_clearing.base_class: New module abmem/services/market/clearing_algorithms/base.py: abstract BaseClearingAlgorithm with ClassVars key, label, description and abstract method clear(self, bids: Sequence[Bid], demand: Decimal, quantum: Decimal) -> ClearingResult. Registration and discovery identical to the agent side (same helper, written once and used by both registries, e.g. abmem/services/plugin_registry.py).
market_clearing.merit_order: The current clear_market logic moves into clearing_algorithms/merit_order.py as MeritOrderClearing (key MERIT_ORDER, label 'Uniform-price merit order'). clearing.py keeps Bid, ClearingResult, acceptance_prices and a thin clear_market wrapper delegating to MERIT_ORDER so the existing tests keep passing.
market_clearing.model: Market.clearing_algorithm = CharField(max_length=64, default='MERIT_ORDER'). Copied by duplicate_scenario and clone_scenario_for_run.
market_clearing.engine: market_service.run_period calls the algorithm of ctx.market.clearing_algorithm (resolved once in SimulationContext.build) and then validate_clearing_result(result, bids, demand, quantum, low, high) before writing anything.
result_contract: accepted has exactly the bid keys
every accepted quantity is a Decimal, 0 <= accepted <= bid quantity and a multiple of quantum
ptf is None iff met_demand == 0, otherwise finite and lowerBidBound <= ptf <= upperBidBound
marginal_group is a subset of the accepted bid keys
A violation raises ClearingContractError (ValueError subclass) naming the algorithm key and the broken rule, and the run fails with that message.
market_clearing.settlement: MarketStrategy (PAYASBID / PAYASPTF) and acceptance_prices stay unchanged and separate from the clearing algorithm.
market_clearing.ui: Scenario wizard market step: a select 'Clearing algorithm' filled from available_clearing_algorithms() with the description as help text, next to the existing settlement rule. Scenario and run detail/list pages show the label. Editing a scenario with an unknown key shows it as unavailable and requires a valid choice.
market_clearing.yaml: scenario YAML market section gains optional key clearing_algorithm (default MERIT_ORDER when missing, validated with is_known_clearing). Export always writes it.

docs: docs/extending_algorithms.md (English): how to add an agent algorithm (subclass, key, config_class with default_search_bounds for HPO, file location) and a clearing algorithm (subclass, contract, file location), with a minimal example of each, and the FORMULATION.md approval rule for research use. Update ARCHITECTURE.md where it describes the registry and the clearing.
tests: Registry: all eight existing keys discovered with correct classes and config classes, ordering, duplicate key error, abstract subclass skipped, a test-only plugin module (created in a tmp package and imported) is discovered for both agents and clearing.
Migration 0017 data mapping int -> key and reverse (MigrationExecutor test or equivalent).
Clearing contract: each rule violated by a fake algorithm raises ClearingContractError, MERIT_ORDER passes on the existing clearing tests.
A run with a test-only clearing algorithm uses it (e.g. a fake that reverses order) and settles with the chosen settlement rule.
Unknown keys: agent and clearing produce SimulationValidationError at build, forms reject them.
Views/YAML: wizard saves clearing_algorithm, YAML round trip with and without the key, algorithm selects show discovered classes, HPO create works with the key.
Grep test: no live module under abmem/ (excluding migrations and enums.py) references AlgorithmType.
Full suite green including the result fingerprint.
out_of_scope: No new clearing or agent algorithm is implemented here besides moving the existing ones.
